Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022 - Study of the Patent Pro Bono Programs The Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022 (the Act or UAIA) required the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to complete a study of the patent pro bono programs. The purpose of the study was to assess the functionality and health of the patent pro bono programs. The Act identified several areas of interest including: Whether the patent pro bono programs are adequately serving prospective and existing participants; Whether any participation requirements of the patent pro bono programs serve as a deterrent for prospective participants; The degree to which prospective inventors are aware of the patent pro bono programs; and Whether the patent pro bono program may benefit from expanding participation to non-attorneys, including patent agents and patent paralegals. Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022 Background The Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022 (UAIA) was signed into law December 29, 2022, and enacted several provisions to better support potential innovators, including establishing a new Southeast Regional Outreach Office, authorizing four new community outreach offices, increasing fee discounts for small and micro entity patent applicants, and authorizing a pre-prosecution pilot program to assist first-time prospective patent applicants. In addition, the UAIA modified the purposes and considerations for establishment of regional outreach offices, as originally set forth in the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act of 2011. The UAIA also directed the USPTO to conduct studies on (1) whether additional regional outreach offices are warranted; (2) the USPTO’s fee structure, with a particular focus on the impact of fee discounts; and (3) the efficacy of patent pro bono programs. pages.text: Unlooted Tombs Shed Light on the Incan Empire's Greatest Rivals | National Geographic By Taylor Mitchell Brown Video by Peru Ministry of Culture Published September 17, 2026 Chan Chan, the capital of the powerful Chimú Empire, was a sprawling, bustling metropolis on the coast of northern Peru some 600 years ago. At its height, it was the largest city in the Americas, spanning nearly eight miles. It boasted complex irrigation canals for farming and teemed with skilled artisans who crafted unparalleled gold and silver metalwork. The city thrived from around A.D. 900 to 1470—when it was conquered by the burgeoning Inca Empire. Now, researchers excavating the city’s ruins have reported a once-in-a-lifetime discovery of unlooted tombs, revealing a new window into the elusive and little-known Chimú elites. The discovery, announced last week by Peru’s Ministry of Culture, will help contextualize previous Chimú findings and reshape archaeologists’ understanding of their enigmatic culture. “Prior to this discovery, what was known about elite Chimú tombs came from platforms that had been looted and destroyed since colonial times,” Jorges Meneses, the archaeologist in charge of the excavation, said in a statement from the Ministry of Culture. From the 38 skeletons and various artifacts he and his colleagues recovered at the site, the archaeologists will now—for the first time—be able to piece together fragmentary evidence of the Chimú elite to better understand how they lived and governed one of Peru’s most formidable empires. pages.text: Updated Candidate Recommendation: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2 | 2026 | News | W3C Skip to content Updated Candidate Recommendation: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2 Author(s) and publish date Published: 6 October 2026 The SVG Working Group invites implementations of an updated Candidate Recommendation Snapshot of Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2 . This is a fresh version of SVG2 with corrections, clarifications and improvements for more interoperability, in particular in implementations in web browsers. This specification defines the features and syntax for Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) Version 2. SVG is a language based on XML for describing two-dimensional vector and mixed vector/raster graphics. SVG content is stylable, scalable to different display resolutions, and can be viewed stand-alone, mixed with HTML content, or embedded using XML namespaces within other XML languages. SVG also supports dynamic changes; script can be used to create interactive documents, and animations can be performed using declarative animation features or by using script. To help the group continue its work in updating this widely-used technology, comments are welcome via Github issues by 1 December 2026 . Related RSS feed Subscribe to our news feed

pages.text: Updating credentials from the macOS Keychain - GitHub Docs Skip to main content Skip to content Collapse sidebar Expand sidebar In this article Updating credentials from the macOS Keychain You'll need to update your saved credentials in the git-credential-osxkeychain helper if you change your username, password, or personal access token on GitHub. Copy markdown In this article Note Updating credentials from the macOS Keychain only applies to users who manually configured a personal access token using the osxkeychain helper that is built-in to macOS. We recommend you either configure SSH or upgrade to the Git Credential Manager (GCM) instead. GCM can manage authentication on your behalf (no more manual personal access tokens) including 2FA (two-factor auth). When Git prompts you for your password, enter your personal access token. Alternatively, you can use a credential helper like Git Credential Manager . Password-based authentication for Git has been removed in favor of more secure authentication methods. For more information, see Managing your personal access tokens . Updating your credentials via Keychain Access Click on the Spotlight icon (magnifying glass) on the right side of the menu bar. Type Keychain Access , then press the Enter key to launch the app. In Keychain Access, search for github.com . Find the "Internet password" entry for github.com . Edit or delete the entry accordingly. With 80 percent of Americans living in cities and suburbs, ensuring they can connect to nature is vital – both to people’s quality of life and the future of conservation. That’s where the Urban Wildlife Conservation Program comes in. Since 2000, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service has partnered with urban and suburban communities to improve residents’ access to nature. Often, these efforts involve urban wildlife refuges — the 100+ national wildlife refuges located within 25 miles of urban areas. Participants in the Urban Bird Treaty , a Service effort combining bird conservation and community improvement, are also frequent partners. To this end, the World Wide Web Consortium makes the following pledge: that as far as possible, for resources on the www.w3.org website which are declared (see below) to be persistent. Pledge Persistent resources will continue to be available throughout the life of the Consortium; Where a persistent resource is modified, a change history will be archived though the archive will not necessarily be available publicly; Should W3C be disbanded, then any website will be granted the right to make a copy (at a different URI) of all public persistent resources so long as they are not modified and are preserved in their entirety and made available free of charge, and provided that the same persistence policy is applied to these "historical mirrors." In such event, the original https://www.w3.org website will be handed over for management to another organization only if that organization pledges to this policy or one considered more persistent. Urinary Tract Infection Basics For Everyone Sept. 22, 2026 Español Key points Do you have pain or burning when you urinate? You might have a urinary tract infection (UTI). UTIs are common infections that happen when bacteria enter the urethra and infect the urinary tract. Antibiotics treat UTIs. A healthcare professional can determine if you have a UTI and what antibiotic you need. Overview The urinary tract includes the bladder, urethra and kidneys (see figure). Urinary tract infections or UTIs are common infections that happen when bacteria, often from the skin or rectum, enter the urethra and infect the urinary tract. pages.text: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers 22 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Madeline Halpert BBC's Madeline Halpert explains why the US lost its measles elimination status and what it could mean. After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. pages.text: US National Security Agency's classified internal network reportedly goes offline Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters US National Security Agency's classified internal network reportedly goes offline 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ana Faguy Getty Images The NSA did not specify which internal services were affected but several media reports say it was the NSANet network A highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communications went offline on Tuesday for an unspecified period of time, according to US media reports. The NSA - America's largest intelligence organisation - said it had experienced a "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance" but that "mission-critical capabilities" were not affected. The outage reportedly affected the NSANet network, which is how officials send and receive top secret or classified information. It comes after a string of technology outages in the US in recent days that have affected flights, banks and other infrastructure. "While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues," an NSA spokesperson said in a statement to the BBC. "NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events." pages.text: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme 7 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Nathan Williams EPA/Shutterstock The US has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme. The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who provides such details. President Donald Trump claimed last year that Iran's nuclear facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated " following a bombing campaign by the US and Israel. Iran insists its nuclear programme is peaceful and that it has no intention of developing a nuclear weapon. Meanwhile, the US military says it is setting up a task force to enhance Washington's efforts to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders. The US military's Central Command (Centcom) said Task Force Iron Gate would operate from Tampa, Florida, and would work with other US government agencies. As well as the movement of weapons, it will also focus on dual-use and illegal revenue streams. Centcom estimates that its naval blockade of Iran's ports has prevented the country from exporting more than $25bn in crude oil.
